Okay veteran preppers. A dead serious prepper newbie is here and I want some answers! (Bug Out Planning)

While you're getting your skills up to snuff, I've got to ask if you're making strong connections with other like minded people or community organizations in your area. The preference for a bug out plan tends to rely on two primary factors. First, that there is no nuclear/biological/chemical warfare in play. Second, that your fall back location is already secured, concealed, stocked, and established. Your best chances for survival will come by not placing all your eggs in one basket. Focus on developing both a bug out plan and a plan to shelter in place. A bug out plan should be a plan of last resort, not the only plan to resort too.

even if you are an avid hunter/trapper, planning on only catching/hunting for food isnt good. you need a food cache. dried grains keep the longest and are compact, rice/pinto/pasta. a 5 gallon bucket with plastic lining (trashbag) and top to seal will work, put some of those descendant packs in there before sealing/hiding, water is the enemy, it'll store for 20 years in ideal conditions, but probably <5. one bucket holds about 80 cups @ 200 calories/cup. you need ~1,200 cal/day doing no work at all, she'll need 1,000cal/day doing no work, the dog if 30lb ankle biter will need 500cal/day resting. so each bucket will feed your group about 4-7 days depending on how you ration it. the rule of thirds is a good rule, estimate the number of days you'll be without additional food, divide into 3rds... consume 2/3rds of your food the first half, and the final 1/3 the last half (that way if you find food early you'll be no worse off). you'll need closer to 2,000 calories if doing labor. if it gets bad, you could do a starvation ration at 400 cal/day, stay in shade move little as possible.
